name: letter-pullup

frames.best_why: Frame 1 shows both lines fully assembled and brightest, with every letter in place.

tagline: Letters rise into place one by one to spell two lines.
summary: Each character of a string rises up into position in sequence, starting transparent and low, so a headline assembles itself letter by letter.
appearance: Two lines of very large sans-serif text sit centred on black: Launch day in white and is finally here in blue. A small Replay button rests in the lower right.
behaviour: On mount every letter starts below and invisible, then springs up into line with a small stagger from left to right. Replay restarts the whole sequence.
demo_content: The words Launch day and is finally here, plus a Replay button.
use_when: A hero headline should arrive with a bit of character instead of a plain fade.
avoid_when: It animates only on mount, so a headline far down the page plays before anyone sees it.
customise: words, delay and className are props; the pull-up distance, font and drop shadow are fixed in the source.
weight_why: One motion element per letter, animating once on mount.

a11y.note: Each letter is its own h1 element, so screen readers may read the headline letter by letter; reduced-motion is ignored.

issues: Each character is rendered as a separate h1 heading, breaking the document outline.
polish_why: Strong type and a pleasant stagger, but it is a very thin one-note effect.
